messages:
Alex: Hey team, customer reported recent CI runs started failing against Redwood API after we rolled service-account token policies yesterday. They see 401s in their build step.

Alex: Error log from their CI job: 
```
REQUEST /v1/deployments/abc123/invoke  401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"token_expired or invalid_scope"}
```

Alex: They use a long-lived CI token created ~18 months ago, scope = [deploy:read,deploy:write,inference:invoke]. We tightened token lifetimes to 90d yesterday which probably expired it. Any quick mitigation?

Deepti: yep that sounds like the TTL change. We pushed a policy that rotates tokens older than 90 days and optional enforcement on non-OIDC tokens. Did we migrate all customers to OIDC?

Alex: Customer hasn't adopted OIDC yet; they rely on service-account tokens stored in GitLab CI secrets. They flagged this as P0 — builds are blocked for one repo owner.

Jon: Quick workaround: we can re-issue a service token for their org with same scopes and TTL extended, but need to confirm least-priv and audit. Also check audit log for token creation to confirm owner.

Alex: They asked for a minimal-perm token — can we create a token limited to just `inference:invoke` for CI jobs that only call the hosted API? If so, how to do it from console/CLI?

Deepti: Yes. From Console -> Team -> Service accounts -> Create token -> uncheck everything except `inference:invoke`. TTL field exposed (90d max for non-OIDC by policy). Alternatively use API: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/service_accounts/tokens \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service_account_id":"sa-789","scopes":["inference:invoke"],"expires_in":7776000}'
```
(7776000s = 90d)

Audrey: Important: if they store token in GitLab CI variables, 90d still means rotation. Recommend using short-lived tokens with automated rotation pipeline, or OIDC passthrough so no static token in repo. We can provide a minimal script to rotate via the API.

Alex: Customer wants hotfix now — can someone create a token for `org:acme` and deliver it to the owner? We should also log consent and add audit note.

Jon: I can create ephemeral token for them and mark as support-temp. Creating now, will scope to `inference:invoke` only and set note: "support: emergency CI unblock - rotate ASAP".

ops-bot: New token created by jon (sa-token-evt): expires 2026-06-18T14:12:30Z, scopes: [inference:invoke]. Audit ID: audit-56321.

Alex: Thanks Jon — passed token to customer via secure channel. They confirmed builds resumed.

Audrey: Follow-up items: 1) Customer migration doc for replacing static service tokens with OIDC 2) Offer a small pipeline snippet to auto-rotate token every 60d and update GitLab secret 3) Make sure our policy email notice triggers for org admins before expiry

Deepti: Also security check: confirm token didn't have `deploy:write` or admin scopes. Jon, can you paste the exact payload you used to create the token? We need to store it in incident ticket.

Jon: Payload I used: 
```
{
  "service_account_id":"sa-acme-01",
  "scopes":["inference:invoke"],
  "expires_in":7776000,
  "note":"support: emergency CI unblock - rotate ASAP"
}
```

security-bot: Reminder: per policy, support-created tokens must be rotated within 7 days and created with MFA-enabled admin keys. Ticket #INC-4521 created for rotation and post-mortem.

Alex: I'll follow up with the customer to schedule OIDC migration and send the rotation reminder. Adding checklist to the ticket: repro steps, logs, token audit id, tmp token expiry.

Audrey: I'll draft the CI rotation snippet, will post to the ticket. Also propose we add a Console UI affordance: `Create temporary token (7d)` that enforces least-priv.

Deepti: Agree — filing an internal feature request. Ticket: FEAT-1319.

Alex: Closing thread for now — builds green. Will ping if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
